data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous topicals & wound care_

**Class:** Porphyrin precursor photosensitiser (5-ALA 20% solution/10% gel; methyl aminolevulinate 16% cream)

## Mechanism of action
- Taken up preferentially by dysplastic/neoplastic and sebaceous cells → converted to protoporphyrin IX
- Light activation (blue 417 nm or red 630 nm, daylight) → reactive oxygen species → selective cell death

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Approved: actinic keratoses (blue light/red light/daylight PDT), superficial BCC and Bowen disease (MAL red light, Europe)
- Off-label: acne, photoageing, sebaceous hyperplasia, warts, actinic cheilitis, field cancerisation in transplant patients

## Dose & formulations
- Apply under occlusion for 1–3 h (incubation), then illuminate (blue 10 J/cm² or red 37 J/cm²); daylight PDT: 30 min incubation then 2 h daylight

## Adverse effects
- Pain/burning during illumination (main limitation), erythema, oedema, crusting, pigmentation; photosensitivity for 24–48 h (avoid sun)

## Contraindications
- Porphyria, photosensitive disorders, allergy to ALA/MAL (peanut/almond oil in MAL cream)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- ALA → protoporphyrin IX → light → ROS
- Blue 417 nm (superficial) vs red 630 nm (deeper)
- Pain during illumination

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.25 (Photodynamic therapy); Khopkar (Photodynamic therapy — blue and red light). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
